 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Nicolas Jackson's form for Aston Villa has been recognised by the Premier League. 
 The 25-year-old has made a positive impact since his £47.5million move from Chelsea, which could rise considerably more.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Jackson has scored eight goals in 12 Premier League and Champions League games combined for Villa this term.
 Six of those goals came in six outings in October, as the Senegal international truly found his feet at Villa Park.
 Jackson has now been nominated for October's Premier League Player of the Month award.
 But history suggests both he and Villa fans should not get too excited just yet.
 Who is up for October's Premier League Player of the Month? 
 The Premier League announced on Friday that Jackson is one of eight players up for the October award.
 Evanilson, Ezri Konsa, Declan Rice, Jack Rudoni, Jan Paul van Hecke, Bart Verbruggen and Luka Vuskovic.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement There are some strong contenders on that list, of course, but Jackson deserves to be in the running.
 In the league, he scored in games against Brentford, Fulham and Manchester City, scoring twice against the latter in a massive win.
 Taking the season as a whole - which admittedly this award is not based off - Jackson has 0.70 goals per 90 in the English top flight.
 That stands him in good stead as one of the hottest strikers around, although Erling Haaland (1.01) will still take some catching.
 Jackson, hailed as "unbelievable" by Peter Crouch in the past, is also registering an average of 0.9 key passes per game, which only four of his Villa teammates can better.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Gary Neville's Nicolas Jackson verdict backed up by Aston Villa stats - but is it sustainable? When did Aston Villa last win Premier League Player of the Month award? 
 The reason Jackson should not be too confident is because Villa players do not win this award very often at all.
 Only nine times have they done so since August 1992, in fact, with seven separate players winning the accolade.
 Remarkably, Christian Benteke was the most recent of those some 11 years ago.
 Despite Villa's success in recent seasons, relatively speaking, the likes of John McGinn, Ollie Watkins and Co. have never landed the award.
 Maybe that will change with Jackson, but do not hold your breath.
